From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Prompt set collection and model-fit next steps (Acme)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get us started on model-fit and prompt evaluation: 

- Goal: Verify model fit for Acme's customer support summarization + redaction flows and collect representative prompts (including edge cases) for our evals.
- Deliverables from Acme: a CSV with ~50 representative prompts (happy path + edge cases), notes on which outputs must be redacted (PII types), and any existing guardrails or post-process rules.
- Redwood deliverables: recommended model(s) to evaluate, a benchmark run on those prompts, suggested prompt templates and redaction guidance, and a short quality/regression checklist.

I've attached a prompt_collection_template.csv to make collection easier — please drop your examples there. A few specific asks:
1) Include examples that contain dates, emails, account IDs, and nested threads (these often break redaction heuristics).
2) Flag rows that are customer PII vs account metadata.
3) If you have API rate/throughput targets, share them so we can prioritize latency-sensitive model variants.

We typically start with two model variants (a high-quality base and a lower-cost quantized variant) and run lightweight evals comparing ROUGE/coverage and a small human pass for hallucination/regression risks. I'll loop in engineering to scope the eval run.

Next steps: Can you upload the filled CSV and any notes by EOD Fri (7/31)? If that timeline doesn't work, tell me the earliest you can.

Thanks — looking forward to the prompts.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>

Hey Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. We'll get the CSV filled — attaching an initial batch of 20 prompts to start (happy paths + a few edge cases). See acme_sample_prompts.csv.

A couple of notes from our side:
- Redaction: anything that includes full account numbers or SSNs must be redacted before sending to external vendors. We can share masked examples (****) and mark the type of PII in a column.
- Legal: they asked to confirm whether Redwood needs access to raw PII for evals. We prefer masked inputs in the first pass; if unmasked inputs are required for fidelity testing, we need a narrow scope and an NDA amendment.
- Throughput: target is 50 req/s peak for API tests; typical latency requirement is p95 < 800ms.

Can Redwood run the benchmark on a masked set and then advise if unmasked testing is necessary? Also, which models do you recommend we evaluate first?

Jordan
Jordan Smith
Product Lead, AI Integrations | Acme Corp
jordan.smith@acme.com

FYI — forwarding Acme's initial prompt batch and legal concern re: raw PII. Jordan asked: can we run the first benchmark on masked inputs and advise if unmasked testing is needed.

Quick asks for you both:
- Vivek: can your team run a light model-fit run on the attached 20 prompts (masked) and send recommended model variants (one high-quality, one quantized/cost-savvy) plus notes on hallucination/regression risk? Please include suggested metrics (automatic + human pass) and an ETA.
- Aditya: can you draft redaction guidance we can send to Acme (what types of PII we can redact safely, examples, and whether masked testing will catch the regressions we care about)? Also flag if we need an NDA amendment for unmasked runs.

I'm asking for a quick turnaround (48 hours) since Acme wants to keep momentum.

—Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Prompt set collection and model-fit next steps (Acme)

Thanks Marissa — we can take this. Initial plan:
1) Run the attached 20 masked prompts through two models: 
   - rwf-xxl-v2 (high-quality base)
   - rwf-xxl-v2-quant8 (latency/cost-optimized)
2) Metrics: token-level latency, p95 latency, ROUGE-L for summarization coverage, hallucination rate (auto heuristics + small human sample), and a regression checklist focused on PII leakage and factual drift.
3) ETA: preliminary report in ~36 hours, full eval + human pass in 5 business days.

On the PII question: masked testing will catch many redaction regressions but not all — things like semantic leakage (where the model infers masked values from context) require targeted unmasked tests under legal review. Aditya, please add formal redaction guidance for the customer note.

I'll upload the benchmarking run and a short notebook to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Acme-benchmarks-XYZ

—Vivek
